decision_register.question: Which source is authoritative for the 2026 standings, the Week 10 slate and the injury designations?
decision_register.known: NFL.com publishes the league standings page, the week schedule page, the rendered injuries page and a dedicated Week 10 injury report article.
decision_register.unknown: Nothing material for the current week.
decision_register.answer: NFL.com only. Every standings, slate and injury value on this site comes from an official NFL page and carries that page's link.
decision_register.discovery_route: Re-read the same pages and compare the SHA of the captured JSON.

decision_register.question: Where do betting lines come from, given that the NFL publishes none?
decision_register.known: The archive at github.com/nflverse/nfldata carries a line, a moneyline and a price for every game.
decision_register.unknown: Nothing about the archive's own provenance of the prices.
decision_register.answer: The archive is used and labelled third-party everywhere. The NFL publishes no betting lines, so no price on this site is officially verifiable and the market cells in official tables stay blank.
decision_register.blocker: No official betting-line source exists. This is a permanent property of the sport, not a gap that can be closed.
decision_register.discovery_route: None available. A sportsbook or a line aggregator would be a commercial third-party source and would still not be official.

decision_register.question: Is the archive's spread_line the home team's line or the away team's line?
decision_register.known: A regression of the actual margin on spread_line has slope +1.04 and intercept -0.04. The moneyline cross check agrees with the away-line reading in 99.41% of 5,432 games.
decision_register.unknown: Nothing that the two checks leave open.
decision_register.answer: The archive's spread_line is the away team's line, so the home line is -spread_line.

decision_register.question: Can the archive's spread and total price columns be used to price a bet?
decision_register.known: The vig-removed probability from the spread prices is anti-calibrated: the games it prices at 0.45 cover 69% of the time and the games it prices at 0.55 cover 45% of the time. The over price sign does not predict the over rate at all.
decision_register.unknown: Why the columns are wrong. The archive does not document the price source.
decision_register.answer: No. The spread strategies use a reference probability reconstructed from the market's moneyline and line, and the total strategies are Blocked because a total has no moneyline to reconstruct from.
decision_register.blocker: The total strategies cannot be priced from any source found.
decision_register.discovery_route: Ask the archive maintainers on github.com/nflverse/nfldata, or find a second archive with a documented price pipeline and test it the same way.
decision_register.status: Closed for the spread strategies. The total strategies stay Blocked.

decision_register.question: Is the pre-registered model as specified fit to use?
decision_register.known: A 3% per-game reversion applied to a mean-zero rating is a multiplicative decay of the whole scale. After one season the rating standard deviation was 1.3 points.
decision_register.unknown: Whether the original author meant per game or per season. The parameter file was written before any run, so there is no evidence either way from the results.
decision_register.answer: The defect was corrected and the correction was selected on the 1999-2022 development window only. The pre-registered variants are still reported as diagnostics.

decision_register.question: May the holdout be scored more than once?
decision_register.known: The holdout is the 2025-2026 season. It was scored with the defective model before the defect was found, then rescored after the correction.
decision_register.answer: The holdout was scored once with the corrected model. The earlier defective-model result is discarded and is not published as a result. The correction was justified on the development window, and the amendment file was committed before the corrected model was scored.
decision_register.blocker: None, provided the amendment is published with the result.
decision_register.discovery_route: The commit order in the history is the evidence.
decision_register.status: Closed. Published openly on the methodology page.

decision_register.question: What can be claimed about a player prop strategy?
decision_register.known: NFL.com publishes no player prop prices and no downloadable player game log was found for the current week.
decision_register.unknown: Nothing that would change the answer.
decision_register.answer: The two player prop strategies are Blocked, not evaluated. No return is reported and no reward is offered.
decision_register.discovery_route: Check the NFL.com stats and player pages for an official game log, and look for a published official prop feed.

decision_register.question: How deep is the replacement starter on the depth chart?
decision_register.known: The official depth chart news names a replacement starter for Baltimore, Arizona, Cleveland and Miami but does not give a depth position. The official game books give a depth position for one quarterback.
decision_register.unknown: The depth position of every other replacement.
decision_register.answer: The depth cell is blank and marked unverified unless an official game book states it.
decision_register.blocker: The official game book for a game exists only after the game is played.
decision_register.discovery_route: Re-read the game book PDF for each Week 10 game once it is published.
decision_register.status: Open. Updates weekly as game books appear.

decision_register.question: Should the eleven prior NFL namespaces be merged into one site?
decision_register.known: They hold 152 HTML pages between them, mostly with source links, and they overlap heavily. The repository audit shows 1,275 table rows without a source link across the repository.
decision_register.unknown: Whether the prior namespaces are still in use by their authors.
decision_register.answer: No merge is performed. This session does not edit any other namespace, and the overlap is recorded so the owner can decide.
decision_register.blocker: The claim in COORDINATION.md reserves this session's scope to nfl-command.
decision_register.discovery_route: Read the claims and verification records in COORDINATION.md.

decision_register.question: Can the model beat the closing line?
decision_register.known: On the holdout the own model's spread error is 10.31 points against the market line's 9.60 and the naive baseline's 10.92.
decision_register.unknown: Whether a materially different model would close the gap.
decision_register.answer: No strategy in the registered family has a verified edge. The betting board pays nothing and the forecast board pays for forecast skill only.
decision_register.blocker: A materially better model would need a different formulation, not a different parameter.
decision_register.status: Closed for this model family. Open as a research question.

decision_register.question: What is the reward currency?
decision_register.known: The reward policy was pre-registered as non-monetary until the owner funds a pool.
decision_register.unknown: The size of any pool and who is paid.

decision_register.question: How much of the archive can be treated as official?
decision_register.known: The archive holds final scores, dates, venues, rest days and lines. NFL.com publishes the same final scores.
decision_register.unknown: Nothing that the reconciliation does not already cover.
decision_register.answer: The 2026 scores reconcile exactly with the official standings page for all 32 teams, so the archive is accepted for scores and rejected for prices.

decision_register.question: Should the site publish the market lines next to the own lines?
decision_register.known: Every market value comes from a third-party archive and no official source publishes a line.
decision_register.answer: The official tables keep the market cells blank. The third-party values appear only in tables that are labelled third-party in the column header and in every row.

decision_register.question: Which of the eleven prior workspaces is the strongest?
decision_register.known: The prior records name nfl-lines as the strongest quantitative candidate, nfl-decision as the questions and suggestions candidate and nfl-hub as the source of the replacement starter game book proof.
decision_register.answer: These are treated as audit candidates, not as verified conclusions. The audit confirms nfl-lines and nfl-decision carry the largest volumes of source-linked tables.
decision_register.blocker: They are outside this session's claim, so they were read and audited but not rewritten.
decision_register.discovery_route: Read the per-file findings in data/derived/repo_audit.json.
decision_register.status: Closed as a reading, open as a consolidation decision.

suggestions.title: Consolidate the eleven prior NFL namespaces into one site
suggestions.option: Choose one canonical NFL site and retire the other ten into an archive
suggestions.evidence: The repository audit found 152 HTML pages across eleven namespaces with 7,001 official links and heavy overlap between nfl-lines, nfl-hub, nfl-decision, nfl-edge and nfl-intel.
suggestions.risk: High. Each namespace has its own verification record and its own provenance file. A merge that breaks a byte-identical rebuild gate would take the site down.
suggestions.prerequisites: Owner approval. A written decision on which namespace is canonical. A link-redirect plan for every published page. A migration that preserves every source link.
suggestions.recommendation: Not recommended inside this change. The overlap is documented; the consolidation is a separate piece of work.

suggestions.title: Add an official player game log so the player prop strategies can be priced
suggestions.option: Capture an official NFL.com player statistics feed for every week and rebuild the prop strategies against it
suggestions.evidence: The prop strategies C1 and C2 are Blocked solely because no official player log and no verifiable prop price were found. The official player pages exist and are linked from the official injury report.
suggestions.risk: Medium. The log would supply the statistic but not the price. Without a price the strategies remain Blocked.
suggestions.prerequisites: A confirmed official statistics endpoint. A decision on whether a third-party prop price is acceptable for settlement.
suggestions.recommendation: Worth doing for the log alone. It also improves the injury and depth tables.

suggestions.title: Replace the rating model with a regression model fitted by maximum likelihood
suggestions.option: Fit a Poisson or negative binomial regression on points scored with team offence, team defence, home field and rest, then read the fitted coefficients as the ratings
suggestions.evidence: The current model reaches a spread error of 10.31 points on the holdout against the market's 9.60. A regression with the same inputs usually beats a hand-built rating because it estimates the weights rather than fixing them.
suggestions.risk: Medium. More parameters means more ways to overfit. The chronological splits and the look-ahead test would have to be extended to cover the extra machinery.
suggestions.prerequisites: A development-window fit with the parameters frozen. The same look-ahead perturbation test. The same ten gates.
suggestions.recommendation: Recommended as the next research step, under a new dated pre-registration, with the holdout untouched until the parameters are frozen.

suggestions.title: Publish the own lines earlier in the week with a wider uncertainty band
suggestions.option: Publish the own line on the Tuesday before the game with an explicit band instead of a point estimate
suggestions.evidence: The holdout own model's 95% band around a predicted margin is roughly plus or minus 13 points, which is wider than almost every published line. The site currently publishes a point and a probability.
suggestions.prerequisites: A published definition of the band and the reference date of the information used.
suggestions.recommendation: Recommended. It makes the honest uncertainty visible next to the number.

suggestions.title: Fund the reward pool
suggestions.option: Set a monetary value per reward point and publish the pool
suggestions.evidence: The reward policy was pre-registered as non-monetary until the owner funds a pool. The forecast board currently pays 221 points across two eligible variants.
suggestions.risk: Low to the analysis. It creates an obligation to keep scoring the holdout honestly.
suggestions.prerequisites: An owner decision on the pool size and on whether the points are paid weekly or at the end of the season.
suggestions.recommendation: Owner decision. No suggestion is auto-approved.

suggestions.title: Add the Week 10 game books to the depth chart table as they appear
suggestions.option: Run the depth chart step weekly and fold each new official game book into the table
suggestions.evidence: The official game books carry the authoritative depth-chart codes. One row is already verified from a game book; the rest are blank because the Week 10 books are not yet published.
suggestions.risk: Low. The step only adds rows that an official document supports.
suggestions.prerequisites: A scheduled run and a check that the published PDF matches the game in question.
suggestions.recommendation: Recommended. It is the only way the depth column can ever be filled from an official source.

suggestions.title: Report the price audit as a standing upstream issue
suggestions.option: Open an issue on github.com/nflverse/nfldata describing the spread and total price columns that fail the calibration test
suggestions.evidence: The spread price columns are anti-calibrated over 5,432 games and the over price sign carries no information over 5,429 games. The failure is reproducible with python3 engine/00_price_audit.py.
suggestions.recommendation: Recommended. It costs nothing and the archive is used widely.

suggestions.title: Add a second third-party price source and test it the same way
suggestions.option: Bring in a second archive with a documented price pipeline and require it to pass the same calibration test before any strategy uses it
suggestions.evidence: The calibration test in engine/00_price_audit.py is the method that caught the defect in the current archive. It would catch the same defect in any source.
suggestions.risk: Medium. A second source means a second reconciliation, and the prices must be reconciled with each other before they can be compared to a model.
suggestions.prerequisites: A second source with a recorded commit and checksum. The same pre-registered audit method.
suggestions.recommendation: Worth doing before the total strategies are unblocked.
